finding.CHECK_INTERNAL_ERROR.detail: An internal error stopped this check, so its result is unknown. Try again later.
finding.CHECK_INTERNAL_ERROR.title: The check could not be completed
finding.CHECK_TIMEOUT.detail: This check did not finish in time, so its result is unknown. Try again later.
finding.CHECK_TIMEOUT.title: The check timed out
finding.CONTENT_EXCESS_CSS.detail: CSS accounts for {css_bytes} of {html_bytes} HTML bytes ({percent}%), at or above the advisory threshold of {threshold}%. Heavy CSS makes the message larger without adding content. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_EXCESS_CSS.remediation: Remove unused styles and simplify repeated inline styles.
finding.CONTENT_EXCESS_CSS.title: CSS takes up most of the HTML
finding.CONTENT_GMAIL_CLIP_RISK.detail: The HTML body is {size} bytes, above the advisory threshold of {threshold} bytes used by this tool. Gmail is commonly reported to clip long messages at around this size. This tool has no official source for this behaviour or this threshold. If a message is clipped, its end, possibly including the unsubscribe link, stays hidden until the reader opens the full message.
finding.CONTENT_GMAIL_CLIP_RISK.remediat: Reduce the size of the HTML, for example by removing unused styles and repeated markup.
finding.CONTENT_GMAIL_CLIP_RISK.title: HTML size above the clipping advisory threshold
finding.CONTENT_HIDDEN_TEXT.detail: {count} element(s) have inline styles that may hide them. These are candidates only, because stylesheets are not evaluated. Content that readers cannot see can look like an attempt to show filters something different.
finding.CONTENT_HIDDEN_TEXT.remediation: Remove content that readers cannot see, unless it is deliberate, such as a preheader.
finding.CONTENT_HIDDEN_TEXT.title: Content that may be hidden
finding.CONTENT_HTTP_ONLY_UNSUBSCRIBE.de: List-Unsubscribe has an http URI but no https URI. The request is not encrypted, and RFC 8058 one-click needs an https URI.
finding.CONTENT_HTTP_ONLY_UNSUBSCRIBE.re: Use an https URL in List-Unsubscribe.
finding.CONTENT_HTTP_ONLY_UNSUBSCRIBE.ti: Unsubscribe link does not use HTTPS
finding.CONTENT_IMAGES_MISSING_ALT.detai: {missing} of {total} image(s) have no alt attribute. Where images are blocked or read aloud by a screen reader, they convey nothing.
finding.CONTENT_IMAGES_MISSING_ALT.remed: Add an alt attribute to every image: a short description, or alt="" for purely decorative images.
finding.CONTENT_IMAGES_MISSING_ALT.title: Images without alternative text
finding.CONTENT_INPUT_CAPPED.detail: Part of the input was over a safety limit or could not be read ({reason}). The results are incomplete and must not be read as a pass.
finding.CONTENT_INPUT_CAPPED.remediation: Provide a smaller or valid message, and make sure it is not corrupted, then analyse it again.
finding.CONTENT_INPUT_CAPPED.title: The content could not be fully analysed
finding.CONTENT_IP_LITERAL_LINK.detail: {count} link(s) point to an IP address instead of a domain name, so readers cannot tell who operates the destination.
finding.CONTENT_IP_LITERAL_LINK.remediat: Use a link on a domain name you control.
finding.CONTENT_IP_LITERAL_LINK.title: Link points to an IP address
finding.CONTENT_LINK_UNEVALUATED.detail: {count} link(s) could not be evaluated because their address could not be read. Their destination and alignment are unknown, so this result is incomplete.
finding.CONTENT_LINK_UNEVALUATED.remedia: Correct the malformed link addresses and analyse the message again.
finding.CONTENT_LINK_UNEVALUATED.title: Some links could not be evaluated
finding.CONTENT_LOW_TEXT_IMAGE_RATIO.det: The HTML has {images} image(s) and {visible_chars} visible characters, about {chars_per_image} per image, below the advisory threshold of {threshold}. When images are not displayed, a message with little text can be unreadable. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_LOW_TEXT_IMAGE_RATIO.rem: Add real text that carries the message, so that it still makes sense without images.
finding.CONTENT_MALFORMED_HTML.detail: The HTML has structural problems: {issues}. Mail clients repair broken markup in different ways, so the message may display differently from what you expect.
finding.CONTENT_MALFORMED_HTML.remediati: Fix the markup in the template and analyse the message again.
finding.CONTENT_MALFORMED_HTML.title: The HTML is malformed
finding.CONTENT_MANY_LINK_DOMAINS.detail: Links point to {count} different domains (not counting the sender domains, when they are known), above the advisory threshold of {threshold}. Many unrelated domains make the message harder to attribute. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_MANY_LINK_DOMAINS.remedi: Reduce the number of different domains, or check that each one is needed.
finding.CONTENT_MANY_LINK_DOMAINS.title: Links point to many different domains
finding.CONTENT_MASKED_LINK.detail: {count} link(s) show one domain in their text but point to another. Readers expect to land where the text says, and this mismatch is also a pattern of phishing messages.
finding.CONTENT_MASKED_LINK.remediation: Make the visible text match the destination, or use descriptive text that shows no domain.
finding.CONTENT_MASKED_LINK.title: Link text shows a different domain
finding.CONTENT_MISSING_PLAIN_TEXT.detai: The input has an HTML body but no plain text version. Readers whose mail client does not display HTML may see little or nothing.
finding.CONTENT_MISSING_PLAIN_TEXT.remed: Send a multipart/alternative message with both a text/plain and a text/html version.
finding.CONTENT_MISSING_PLAIN_TEXT.title: No plain text version
finding.CONTENT_NON_HTTPS_LINK.detail: {count} link(s) use http:// instead of https://, so the connection is not encrypted and can be altered in transit.
finding.CONTENT_NON_HTTPS_LINK.remediati: Serve those pages over HTTPS and update the links.
finding.CONTENT_NON_HTTPS_LINK.title: Link does not use HTTPS
finding.CONTENT_NO_LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE.deta: No List-Unsubscribe header was found in the message. For one-to-one or transactional mail this can be fine; for bulk or marketing mail it makes unsubscribing harder (RFC 2369).
finding.CONTENT_NO_LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE.reme: For bulk mail, add a List-Unsubscribe header with an https link or a mailto address.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.detail: List-Unsubscribe is present but List-Unsubscribe-Post is missing, so one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) is not offered.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.detail_dupl: List-Unsubscribe or List-Unsubscribe-Post appears more than once. RFC 8058 expects exactly one of each, so one-click unsubscribe cannot be relied on.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.detail_no_h: List-Unsubscribe-Post is present, but List-Unsubscribe has no valid https URI. RFC 8058 requires one, so one-click unsubscribe is not offered.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.detail_nons: The https URI in List-Unsubscribe is not written in the standard https://host form (RFC 3986), so it does not count for one-click unsubscribe.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.detail_post: List-Unsubscribe-Post is not exactly List-Unsubscribe=One-Click. It may be invalid or differ only by letter case; do not depend on how a receiver compares it (RFC 8058).
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.remediation: Send exactly one List-Unsubscribe with a standard https URL and exactly one List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click.
finding.CONTENT_NO_ONE_CLICK.title: One-click unsubscribe is not offered
finding.CONTENT_RULE_ERROR.detail: {count} content rule(s) failed or did not finish ({reasons}), so the rule results are incomplete. A low score here does not mean the content is clean.
finding.CONTENT_RULE_ERROR.remediation: Analyse the message again. If the problem persists, ask an administrator to check the rules named here.
finding.CONTENT_RULE_ERROR.title: Some content rules could not be evaluated
finding.CONTENT_RULE_MATCH.detail: The rule "{rule}" (category {category}, weight {weight}) matched in: {part}. Rules are configurable signals of this tool: a match does not say how a receiver will treat the message.
finding.CONTENT_RULE_MATCH.remediation: Review the matched text and reword it if the rule applies to this message.
finding.CONTENT_RULE_MATCH.title: Content rule matched: {rule}
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_ALL_CAPS.detail: {percent}% of the letters in the Subject are capitals, which this tool flags as an advisory heuristic: text in capitals reads as shouting. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_ALL_CAPS.remedia: Write the Subject in normal sentence case.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_ALL_CAPS.title: Subject is mostly capitals
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_BIDI_OVERRIDE.de: The Subject contains {count} bidirectional control character(s), including overrides. They can make the displayed text differ from the characters actually sent.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_BIDI_OVERRIDE.re: Remove the direction override characters from the Subject.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_CONTROL_CHARS.de: The Subject contains {count} control character(s). They have no visible meaning and can be a sign of a broken template or of header injection.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_CONTROL_CHARS.re: Remove the control characters and check how the Subject is generated.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_EMPTY.detail: The message has no Subject, or its Subject shows nothing. Readers get no idea of what the message is about.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_EMPTY.remediatio: Add a Subject that describes the message.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_EMPTY.title: The Subject is missing or blank
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_LONG.detail: The Subject is about {length} characters long, over the advisory limit this tool uses. Long subjects can be cut off in message lists, depending on the client. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_LONG.remediation: Shorten the Subject and put the key information first.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_LONG.title: Subject is long
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_MIXED_SCRIPT.det: A word in the Subject mixes letters of different scripts ({scripts}). Look-alike letters can disguise a word.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_MIXED_SCRIPT.rem: Check that every word of the Subject uses one script.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_PUNCTUATION.deta: The Subject has a run of {run} exclamation or question marks, which this tool flags as an advisory heuristic: repeated punctuation can look pushy. This tool has no official source for this threshold.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_PUNCTUATION.reme: Use at most one punctuation mark in a row.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_REPLY_PREFIX.det: The Subject starts with the prefix "{prefix}", but the message has no In-Reply-To or References header. A prefix that suggests an earlier conversation can mislead readers if there was none.
finding.CONTENT_SUBJECT_REPLY_PREFIX.rem: Remove the prefix unless the message is a real reply.
finding.CONTENT_UNALIGNED_LINK_DOMAIN.de: {count} link(s) point to a domain other than the sender domains ({senders}); {unevaluated} link(s) could not be checked. Links to unrelated domains make it harder to see who is behind the message, although the tracking domain of a sending service can explain them.
finding.CONTENT_UNALIGNED_LINK_DOMAIN.re: Where your sending service supports it, use links on your own domain, for example a branded tracking domain.
finding.CONTENT_UNALIGNED_LINK_DOMAIN.ti: Link domain differs from the sender
finding.CONTENT_UNSIGNED_UNSUBSCRIBE_HEA: No DKIM-Signature lists both List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post in its h= tag. RFC 8058 requires a valid DKIM signature covering both, and says that one-click should not be offered without it. Signatures are not verified here.
Configure your sending service to include List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post in the DKIM signature.
Unsubscribe headers are not covered by DKIM
finding.CONTENT_URL_SHORTENER.detail: {count} link(s) use a domain on this tool's list of URL shorteners. A shortener hides the final destination from the reader.
finding.CONTENT_URL_SHORTENER.remediatio: Link directly to the destination, on a domain you control.
finding.CONTENT_URL_SHORTENER.title: Link uses a URL shortener
finding.CUSTOM_CHECK_ERROR.detail: Custom check {check_key} could not be evaluated (reason: {reason}). Nothing can be concluded about the record.
finding.CUSTOM_CHECK_ERROR.title: Custom check could not be evaluated
finding.CUSTOM_CHECK_FAILED.detail: Custom check {check_key} did not pass for the {rrtype} records of {name} (reason: {reason}).
finding.CUSTOM_CHECK_FAILED.title: Custom check did not pass
finding.CUSTOM_KIND_UNAVAILABLE.detail: Custom check {check_key} uses a kind that is not available yet, so it was not run.
finding.CUSTOM_KIND_UNAVAILABLE.title: Custom check kind not available yet
finding.DKIM_CNAME_CHAIN_LONG.detail: The CNAME chain from {name} (selector {selector}) is longer than {max} hops, so we stopped following it and could not evaluate the selector.
finding.DKIM_CNAME_CHAIN_LONG.remediatio: Shorten the delegation chain or point the CNAME directly at the key record.
finding.DKIM_CNAME_CHAIN_LONG.title: CNAME chain too long at a DKIM selector
finding.DKIM_CNAME_LOOP.detail: Following the CNAME chain from {name} (selector {selector}) returns to a name already visited, so the key cannot be reached.
finding.DKIM_CNAME_LOOP.remediation: Fix the delegation so the CNAME chain ends at the key record provided by your sending service.
finding.DKIM_CNAME_LOOP.title: CNAME loop at a DKIM selector
finding.DKIM_KEY_REVOKED.detail: The record at {name} (selector {selector}) has an empty p tag, which means the key was revoked. Messages signed with this selector fail DKIM verification.
finding.DKIM_KEY_REVOKED.remediation: If the selector is still in use, publish a new key; if it is retired, no action is needed.
finding.DKIM_KEY_REVOKED.title: DKIM key is revoked
finding.DKIM_KEY_SYNTAX_ERROR.detail: The record at {name} (selector {selector}) cannot be used by a verifier because of syntax or key errors (see evidence).
finding.DKIM_KEY_SYNTAX_ERROR.remediatio: Republish the key record exactly as provided by your sending service, as a single TXT record without extra characters.
finding.DKIM_KEY_SYNTAX_ERROR.title: DKIM key record is invalid
finding.DKIM_KEY_TOO_SHORT.detail: The RSA key at {name} (selector {selector}) is {bits} bits. RFC 8301 says verifiers must not accept RSA keys shorter than 1024 bits.
finding.DKIM_KEY_TOO_SHORT.remediation: Replace it with a 2048-bit RSA key following your sending service's instructions.
finding.DKIM_KEY_TOO_SHORT.title: DKIM RSA key is shorter than 1024 bits
finding.DKIM_KEY_WEAK_1024.detail: The RSA key at {name} (selector {selector}) is {bits} bits. RFC 8301 allows it but recommends signers use 2048-bit keys.
finding.DKIM_KEY_WEAK_1024.remediation: Rotate to a 2048-bit RSA key (or Ed25519 alongside RSA) following your sending service's instructions.
finding.DKIM_KEY_WEAK_1024.title: DKIM RSA key is 1024 bits
finding.DKIM_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.detail: More than one TXT record exists at {name} (selector {selector}). Verifiers expect a single key record, so the result can be ambiguous.
finding.DKIM_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.remediatio: Keep a single key record at this name and remove the others.
finding.DKIM_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.title: Several TXT records at a DKIM selector
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTORS_PROBED.detail: The selector list for this domain is empty, for example because every selector is disabled, so nothing was looked up in DNS. This result says nothing about whether the domain uses DKIM.
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTORS_PROBED.remedia: Enable at least one DKIM selector, or add the selectors your sending services use, and run the check again.
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTORS_PROBED.title: No DKIM selectors were probed
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTOR_FOUND.detail: None of the {count} selectors we tried returned a DKIM key record. This does not show that DKIM is missing: selectors cannot be enumerated in DNS, and your sending service may use a selector name that is not in our list.
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTOR_FOUND.remediati: Add the selector names your sending services actually use (the s= tag of the DKIM-Signature header in a message you sent shows it) and run the check again.
finding.DKIM_NO_SELECTOR_FOUND.title: No DKIM key found among the selectors tried
finding.DKIM_PROBE_ERRORS.detail: {count} of {total} selectors could not be evaluated because of DNS errors or malformed delegations (see evidence). One of them may be the selector you actually use, so the result is incomplete.
finding.DKIM_PROBE_ERRORS.remediation: Retry the check later; if the same selectors keep failing, check the DNS configuration of the domain and of any CNAME targets.
finding.DKIM_PROBE_ERRORS.title: Some DKIM selectors could not be evaluated
finding.DKIM_SELECTORS_CAPPED.detail: {dropped} selectors were skipped because a probe covers at most {probed} selectors, so the result is incomplete. One of the skipped selectors may be the one you actually use.
finding.DKIM_SELECTORS_CAPPED.remediatio: Remove or disable the selectors you do not need and run the check again.
finding.DKIM_SELECTORS_CAPPED.title: Some DKIM selectors were not probed
finding.DKIM_TEST_MODE.detail: The record at {name} (selector {selector}) has the t=y flag, which tells verifiers the domain is testing DKIM. Some receivers treat such signatures differently.
finding.DKIM_TEST_MODE.remediation: Remove the y flag from the t tag once DKIM signing is verified and live.
finding.DKIM_TEST_MODE.title: DKIM key is in testing mode
finding.DMARC_ALIGNMENT_STRICT.detail: The record uses strict alignment (adkim={adkim}, aspf={aspf}), which requires an exact domain match instead of the same organizational domain.
finding.DMARC_ALIGNMENT_STRICT.remediati: Make sure all legitimate senders use the exact From domain, or use relaxed alignment (r).
finding.DMARC_ALIGNMENT_STRICT.title: Strict alignment configured
finding.DMARC_DNS_ERROR.detail: The DNS lookup for {name} failed (state: {state}), so the DMARC status is unknown. This is not the same as having no record.
finding.DMARC_DNS_ERROR.remediation: Retry later and check that the domain's name servers answer correctly.
finding.DMARC_DNS_ERROR.title: DMARC could not be checked
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_AUTH_RECORD_INVAL: The authorization record for {destination} at {query} has syntax errors.
Ask the operator of {destination} to correct the record at {query}; a record containing only "v=DMARC1" is enough.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_AUTH_RECORD_UNPAR: A record starting with v=DMARC1 was found for {destination} at {query}, but it could not be parsed as a tag=value list (for example, an empty or invalid tag). It is ignored, so {destination} is not authorized and these reports will likely be dropped.
Ask the operator of {destination} to correct the record at {query}; a record containing only "v=DMARC1" is enough.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_AUTH_UNVERIFIED.d: The DNS lookup for {query} failed (state: {state}), so it is unknown whether {destination} accepts reports for this domain. This is not the same as a missing authorization.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_AUTH_UNVERIFIED.r: Retry later and check that the name servers of {destination} answer correctly.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_AUTH_UNVERIFIED.t: External report destination could not be checked
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_NOT_CHECKABLE.det: The report URI {uri} does not name a single destination host (for example, it lists several addresses), so its authorization cannot be verified and it is not counted as authorized.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_NOT_CHECKABLE.rem: List each report address as its own mailto URI; separate the URIs with commas in the rua or ruf tag.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_OVERRIDE_MISMATCH: The authorization record for {destination} at {query} exists, but it overrides the report address with a URI on a different host. Under RFC 7489 section 7.1, receivers then send no reports to either the original or the override address.
Ask the operator of {destination} to remove the override from the record at {query}, or to correct it so that it uses {destination}.
Report destination override points to another host
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_TOO_MANY_DESTINAT: The record lists {count} external report destinations; only the first {limit} were checked.
Reduce the report addresses in rua and ruf to the ones you actually use.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_UNAUTHORIZED.deta: Reports are requested at {destination}, outside your organizational domain, but no valid authorization record was found at {query}. Receivers following RFC 7489 ignore this address, so these reports will likely be dropped.
finding.DMARC_EXTERNAL_UNAUTHORIZED.reme: Ask the operator of {destination} to publish a TXT record "v=DMARC1" at {query}, or use a report address within your own domain.
finding.DMARC_INHERITED_FROM_ORG.detail: No DMARC record exists at this subdomain; the record of {found_at} was used (RFC 7489 section 6.6.3).
finding.DMARC_INHERITED_FROM_ORG.remedia: To set a separate policy for this subdomain, publish a DMARC record at _dmarc.<subdomain>.
finding.DMARC_INHERITED_FROM_ORG.title: DMARC record inherited from the organizational domain
finding.DMARC_MISSING.detail: No DMARC record was found at _dmarc for this domain or, for a subdomain, for its organizational domain.
finding.DMARC_MISSING.remediation: Publish a TXT record at _dmarc.<domain> starting with v=DMARC1 and containing a p tag; p=none with a rua address is a common way to start collecting reports.
finding.DMARC_MISSING.title: No DMARC record found
finding.DMARC_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.detail: More than one TXT record starting with v=DMARC1 exists at {name}. RFC 7489 section 6.6.3 says policy discovery then terminates and DMARC processing is not applied.
finding.DMARC_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.remediati: Keep a single DMARC record at this name and remove the others.
finding.DMARC_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.title: Multiple DMARC records
finding.DMARC_NO_RUA.detail: The record has no valid rua tag, so no aggregate reports are requested.
finding.DMARC_NO_RUA.remediation: Add rua=mailto:<address> to receive aggregate reports.
finding.DMARC_NO_RUA.title: No aggregate report address
finding.DMARC_NO_USABLE_POLICY.detail: The record has no valid p tag (or has an invalid sp tag) and no valid rua address. Per RFC 7489 section 6.6.3 receivers then apply no DMARC processing.
finding.DMARC_NO_USABLE_POLICY.remediati: Add a valid p tag (none, quarantine or reject) and a rua address.
finding.DMARC_NO_USABLE_POLICY.title: No usable DMARC policy
finding.DMARC_PCT_PARTIAL.detail: pct={pct} means the {p} policy is requested for only that percentage of messages (RFC 7489 section 6.3).
finding.DMARC_PCT_PARTIAL.remediation: Once reports look clean, raise pct to 100 or remove the tag (the default is 100).
finding.DMARC_PCT_PARTIAL.title: Policy applies to a percentage of messages
finding.DMARC_POLICY_NONE.detail: The policy is p=none: it requests monitoring only and no action on messages that fail DMARC.
finding.DMARC_POLICY_NONE.remediation: After reviewing aggregate reports, consider moving to p=quarantine and then p=reject.
finding.DMARC_POLICY_NONE.title: DMARC policy is none
finding.DMARC_POLICY_QUARANTINE.detail: The policy is p=quarantine: it requests that messages failing DMARC be treated as suspicious.
finding.DMARC_POLICY_QUARANTINE.remediat: If reports show that legitimate mail passes, p=reject is the strictest policy.
finding.DMARC_POLICY_QUARANTINE.title: DMARC policy is quarantine
finding.DMARC_P_ASSUMED_NONE.detail: The record has no valid p tag (or has an invalid sp tag) but has a valid rua address. Per RFC 7489 section 6.6.3 receivers SHOULD act as if p=none was retrieved.
finding.DMARC_P_ASSUMED_NONE.remediation: Add a valid p tag (none, quarantine or reject) and fix any invalid sp tag.
finding.DMARC_P_ASSUMED_NONE.title: Missing or invalid p: receivers apply p=none
finding.DMARC_RUF_PRESENT.detail: The record requests failure reports with the ruf tag. This check does not verify whether any receiver sends them.
finding.DMARC_RUF_PRESENT.remediation: Do not rely on ruf alone; use aggregate reports (rua) for monitoring. Make sure the destination can handle message data.
finding.DMARC_RUF_PRESENT.title: Failure report address (ruf) present
finding.DMARC_SUBDOMAIN_POLICY_WEAKER.de: The sp tag ({sp}) is weaker than the p tag ({p}), so subdomains are covered by a less strict policy than the domain itself.
finding.DMARC_SUBDOMAIN_POLICY_WEAKER.re: Remove sp so that p applies to subdomains, or set sp to a policy at least as strict as p.
finding.DMARC_SUBDOMAIN_POLICY_WEAKER.ti: Subdomain policy is weaker than the domain policy
finding.DMARC_SYNTAX_ERROR.detail: The DMARC record does not follow the syntax of RFC 7489 section 6.3. The issues found are listed as evidence.
finding.DMARC_SYNTAX_ERROR.remediation: Correct the listed tags. Tags other than v and p that are invalid may be discarded in favour of defaults (RFC 7489 section 6.3).
finding.DMARC_SYNTAX_ERROR.title: DMARC record has syntax errors
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_FAIL.detail: Neither the SPF nor a DKIM identifier is aligned with the From domain {from_domain}. Domains seen: {identifiers}. This was computed here from the stated results.
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_FAIL.remediation: Send with a Return-Path or a DKIM d= domain that shares the organizational domain of the From address.
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_FAIL.title: No identifier is aligned with the From domain
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_STATED_MISMATCH.de: The receiver wrote dmarc={stated}, but the alignment computed here gives the opposite result. The header may be forged, or the receiver may know a policy that is not visible here.
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_STATED_MISMATCH.re: Do not rely on this Authentication-Results header; compare it with the one added by your own receiving server.
finding.MSG_ALIGNMENT_STATED_MISMATCH.ti: The stated DMARC result disagrees with the computed one
finding.MSG_ARC_CV_FAIL.detail: An ARC-Seal says cv=fail, meaning an intermediary declared that the earlier chain did not validate. This was not re-checked here.
finding.MSG_ARC_CV_FAIL.remediation: Find the intermediary that sealed the chain as failed and check what it changed or how it validated the previous hop.
finding.MSG_ARC_CV_FAIL.title: An ARC seal reports a failed chain
finding.MSG_ARC_INVALID.detail: The ARC headers are malformed or numbered incorrectly. Signatures are not verified here, so a valid-looking chain proves nothing either.
finding.MSG_ARC_INVALID.remediation: Check the intermediaries that add ARC headers: instances must start at 1, be contiguous and be complete.
finding.MSG_ARC_INVALID.title: The ARC chain is structurally invalid
finding.MSG_AUTHRES_AUTHSERV_MISMATCH.de: The results used here carry {count} different authserv-ids ({ids}). Authentication-Results can be written by anyone upstream, so none of them is trusted.
finding.MSG_AUTHRES_AUTHSERV_MISMATCH.re: Look only at results added by the server that received the message into your own infrastructure, and ignore the others.
finding.MSG_AUTHRES_MISSING.detail: No Authentication-Results header was found, so SPF, DKIM and DMARC results are not available. This is not a pass.
finding.MSG_AUTHRES_MISSING.remediation: Provide a copy of the message as stored by the receiving mailbox, which includes the receiver's Authentication-Results.
finding.MSG_AUTHRES_MISSING.title: No Authentication-Results header
finding.MSG_DATE_FAR_FROM_RECEIVED.detai: The Date header differs by about {skew_hours} hours from the time of the first Received hop (limit {max_hours} hours). A wrong clock or a rewritten header can cause this.
finding.MSG_DATE_FAR_FROM_RECEIVED.remed: Check the clock of the sending system and make sure nothing rewrites the Date header.
finding.MSG_DATE_FAR_FROM_RECEIVED.title: The Date header is far from the first hop time
finding.MSG_DATE_INVALID.detail: The Date header is not a valid RFC 5322 date, so its time could not be evaluated.
finding.MSG_DATE_INVALID.remediation: Generate the Date header with your mail library using the RFC 5322 format, for example Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:15:00 +0000.
finding.MSG_DATE_INVALID.title: The Date header cannot be parsed
finding.MSG_DATE_NO_TIMEZONE.detail: The Date header has no time zone, so its time cannot be compared with the delivery chain. No zone is assumed.
finding.MSG_DATE_NO_TIMEZONE.remediation: Add a numeric time zone offset such as +0000 to the Date header.
finding.MSG_DATE_NO_TIMEZONE.title: The Date header has no time zone
finding.MSG_DKIM_NOT_PASS.detail: No stated DKIM result is pass (stated: {result}). The results are what the receiver wrote and have not been re-checked here.
finding.MSG_DKIM_NOT_PASS.detail_not_sta: No DKIM result is stated in Authentication-Results, so DKIM could not be evaluated. This is not a pass.
finding.MSG_DKIM_NOT_PASS.remediation: Sign outgoing mail with DKIM and make sure the public key is published in DNS.
finding.MSG_DKIM_NOT_PASS.title: No DKIM signature passed
finding.MSG_DMARC_NOT_PASS.detail: The stated DMARC result is: {result}. The result is what the receiver wrote and has not been re-checked here.
finding.MSG_DMARC_NOT_PASS.detail_not_st: No DMARC result is stated in Authentication-Results, so DMARC could not be evaluated. This is not a pass.
finding.MSG_DMARC_NOT_PASS.remediation: Make sure SPF or DKIM passes and aligns with the domain in the From header.
finding.MSG_DMARC_NOT_PASS.title: DMARC did not pass
finding.MSG_DUPLICATE_SINGLETON_HEADER.d: The {header} header appears {count} times, but RFC 5322 section 3.6 allows it only once.
finding.MSG_DUPLICATE_SINGLETON_HEADER.r: Remove the duplicate {header} headers so that only one remains.
finding.MSG_DUPLICATE_SINGLETON_HEADER.t: A header that must appear once is repeated
finding.MSG_ENCODED_HEADER_BROKEN.detail: {count} RFC 2047 encoded-word(s) in the headers could not be decoded, so some header text may be shown wrongly.
finding.MSG_ENCODED_HEADER_BROKEN.remedi: Encode non-ASCII header text with a valid charset and well-formed encoded-words, or let your mail library do it.
finding.MSG_ENCODED_HEADER_BROKEN.title: Broken encoded header text
finding.MSG_HOP_DELAY_HIGH.detail: Hop {hop} added a delay of {delay_seconds} seconds, above the {threshold_seconds} second threshold. Queueing, retries or deferrals can cause this.
finding.MSG_HOP_DELAY_HIGH.remediation: Check the queue and retry logs of the relay involved to find out why the message waited.
finding.MSG_HOP_DELAY_HIGH.title: A hop took a long time
finding.MSG_LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE_MISSING.det: No List-Unsubscribe header was found. For one-to-one or transactional mail this is fine; for bulk or marketing mail it makes unsubscribing harder (RFC 2369).
finding.MSG_LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE_MISSING.rem: For bulk mail, add a List-Unsubscribe header with an https link or a mailto address.
finding.MSG_LIST_UNSUBSCRIBE_NO_ONECLICK: List-Unsubscribe is present but List-Unsubscribe-Post with List-Unsubscribe=One-Click is not, so one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) is not offered.
To offer one-click unsubscribe, add List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click and an https URL in List-Unsubscribe.
finding.MSG_MIME_TRUNCATED.detail: The MIME structure exceeds the analysis limits, so only part of it was examined and later parts are not reported.
finding.MSG_MIME_TRUNCATED.remediation: Simplify the message structure (fewer nested or repeated parts) and test again.
finding.MSG_MIME_TRUNCATED.title: The MIME structure was only partly read
finding.MSG_MISSING_DATE.detail: No Date header was found, or it is empty, so the sending time cannot be checked against the delivery chain.
finding.MSG_MISSING_DATE.remediation: Add a Date header in the RFC 5322 format, including the time zone.
finding.MSG_MISSING_DATE.title: The message has no Date header
finding.MSG_MISSING_FROM.detail: No From header was found, or it is empty. The sender identity cannot be determined and alignment cannot be evaluated.
finding.MSG_MISSING_FROM.remediation: Add exactly one From header with the visible sender address (RFC 5322 section 3.6).
finding.MSG_MISSING_FROM.title: The message has no From header
finding.MSG_MISSING_MESSAGE_ID.detail: No Message-ID header was found, or it is empty. Receivers expect one unique identifier per message (RFC 5322 section 3.6.4).
finding.MSG_MISSING_MESSAGE_ID.remediati: Add a unique Message-ID header, with a domain you control, to every message.
finding.MSG_MISSING_MESSAGE_ID.title: The message has no Message-ID header
finding.MSG_MULTIPLE_FROM.detail: {count} From headers were found. RFC 5322 allows only one, and receivers may treat the message differently from how you expect.
finding.MSG_MULTIPLE_FROM.remediation: Remove the extra From headers so that only one remains.
finding.MSG_MULTIPLE_FROM.title: The message has more than one From header
finding.MSG_NO_TEXT_PART.detail: The message has no text/plain part. HTML-only messages are harder to read in some clients and are more often treated with suspicion.
finding.MSG_NO_TEXT_PART.remediation: Send a multipart/alternative message with both a text/plain and a text/html version.
finding.MSG_NO_TEXT_PART.title: No plain text part
finding.MSG_PARSER_LIMIT.detail: The message was rejected or only partly analysed because of safety limits. Results are incomplete and must not be read as a pass.
finding.MSG_PARSER_LIMIT.remediation: Provide a smaller message or only its headers, and make sure it is not corrupted.
finding.MSG_PARSER_LIMIT.title: The input exceeded analysis limits
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_CLOCK_SKEW.detail: {count} hop(s) are timestamped earlier than the previous hop. Clocks that are out of sync or forged Received headers can cause this.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_CLOCK_SKEW.remediat: Synchronise the clocks of the relays you control (NTP) and review the hops involved.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_CLOCK_SKEW.title: The Received timestamps go backwards
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_NONE.detail: No Received header was found, so the delivery chain, hop delays and clock skew could not be evaluated. Messages captured before any relay handled them look like this.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_NONE.remediation: Provide the full raw message as it was delivered, including all Received headers.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_NONE.title: The message has no Received headers
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_PRIVATE_IP_ORIGIN.d: The first Received hop shows the address {ip}, which is not a public internet address. This is normal for internal submission, but the original client is not visible.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_PRIVATE_IP_ORIGIN.r: If this is unexpected, check which system submitted the message and how it reaches your relay.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_PRIVATE_IP_ORIGIN.t: The first hop has a non-public address
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_UNPARSED.detail: {unparsed} of {total} Received headers could not be parsed, so the chain is only partly evaluated.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_UNPARSED.remediatio: Check that the Received headers were not altered or truncated when the message was exported.
finding.MSG_RECEIVED_UNPARSED.title: Some Received headers could not be parsed
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.detail: The Reply-To domain ({reply_to_domain}) belongs to a different organization than the From domain ({from_domain}). This is often intentional.
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.remediation: If it is not intentional, make Reply-To use the same domain as From or remove it.
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_DIFFERS.title: Reply-To uses a different domain
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_UNUSABLE.detail: A Reply-To header is present but contains no valid address with a usable domain, so it could not be compared with the From domain.
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_UNUSABLE.remediatio: Set Reply-To to a single valid address, or remove the header.
finding.MSG_REPLY_TO_UNUSABLE.title: Reply-To has no usable address
finding.MSG_RETURN_PATH_MISSING.detail: No Return-Path header was found. It is normally added by the final receiving server, so a copy taken earlier will not have it, and the bounce address cannot be checked.
finding.MSG_RETURN_PATH_MISSING.remediat: Use a copy of the message as stored by the receiving mailbox if you need to inspect the bounce address.
finding.MSG_RETURN_PATH_MISSING.title: No Return-Path header
finding.MSG_SPF_NOT_PASS.detail: The stated SPF result is: {result}. The result is what the receiver wrote and has not been re-checked here.
finding.MSG_SPF_NOT_PASS.detail_not_stat: No SPF result is stated in Authentication-Results, so SPF could not be evaluated. This is not a pass.
finding.MSG_SPF_NOT_PASS.remediation: Make sure the sending IP is authorised by the SPF record of the envelope sender domain.
finding.MSG_SPF_NOT_PASS.title: SPF did not pass
finding.MSG_UNVERIFIED_DKIM_SIGNATURE.de: {count} DKIM-Signature header(s) have no matching result in Authentication-Results (domains: {domains}). The signatures were not verified here.
finding.MSG_UNVERIFIED_DKIM_SIGNATURE.re: Check why the receiver did not report a result for these signatures, for example a missing key or a signature added after receipt.
finding.MSG_UNVERIFIED_DKIM_SIGNATURE.ti: DKIM signatures without a stated result
finding.SPF_DNS_ERROR.detail: The SPF result could not be determined because a DNS lookup failed: {rdtype} for {name} (state: {state}). This is not the same as having no record.
finding.SPF_DNS_ERROR.remediation: Retry later and check that the name servers for the failing name answer correctly.
finding.SPF_DNS_ERROR.title: SPF could not be checked
finding.SPF_FLATTENING_HINT.detail: The SPF tree uses {count} of {limit} DNS lookups. The evidence lists the includes ranked by how many lookups each consumes, including everything below it.
finding.SPF_FLATTENING_HINT.remediation: Start with the most expensive includes: remove services that no longer send mail, or move some senders to a subdomain. Flattening (replacing an include with the IP addresses it currently resolves to) lowers the lookup count but trades it for maintenance burden: providers can change their addresses at any time, and a stale flattened record silently breaks SPF. Only flatten with a process that keeps the addresses up to date.
finding.SPF_FLATTENING_HINT.title: Ways to reduce SPF lookups
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_LOOP.detail: {name} is reached again through a {via} chain that already contains it. A receiver following it can only stop at the DNS lookup limit, which gives permerror (RFC 7208 section 4.6.4).
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_LOOP.remediation: Remove the include or redirect that points back to a record already in the chain.
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_LOOP.title: SPF include or redirect loop
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_NOT_FOUND.detail: The {via} target {name} has no SPF record. RFC 7208 sections 5.2 and 6.1 make this a permerror for the whole evaluation, not a simple no-match.
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_NOT_FOUND.remediatio: Correct the target name, or remove the term if the service no longer publishes an SPF record there.
finding.SPF_INCLUDE_NOT_FOUND.title: SPF include or redirect target has no SPF record
finding.SPF_MISSING.detail: No TXT record starting with v=spf1 was found at {domain}. Receivers get the SPF result "none" (RFC 7208 sections 2.6.1 and 4.5).
finding.SPF_MISSING.remediation: Publish one TXT record at the domain starting with v=spf1 that lists the hosts allowed to send for it and ends with an all mechanism, for example -all or ~all. If the domain sends no mail, publish v=spf1 -all.
finding.SPF_MISSING.title: No SPF record found
finding.SPF_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.detail: {name} publishes {count} TXT records starting with v=spf1. RFC 7208 section 4.5 requires exactly one; with more than one, receivers return permerror.
finding.SPF_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.remediation: Merge the records into a single v=spf1 record at this name and delete the others.
finding.SPF_MULTIPLE_RECORDS.title: Multiple SPF records
finding.SPF_MX_TOO_MANY_HOSTS.detail: The term {term} in the SPF record at {name} resolves to {count} MX hosts. RFC 7208 section 4.6.4: evaluating an mx mechanism MUST NOT query more than {limit} address records; if this limit is exceeded, the mx mechanism MUST produce a permerror result.
finding.SPF_MX_TOO_MANY_HOSTS.remediatio: Replace this mx term with ip4/ip6 ranges or a terms for the hosts that actually send mail, or reduce the MX hosts of the target name to {limit} or fewer.
finding.SPF_MX_TOO_MANY_HOSTS.title: SPF mx term points to too many hosts
finding.SPF_NEAR_LOOKUP_LIMIT.detail: Evaluating the SPF record needs {count} DNS-querying terms, close to the limit of {limit} in RFC 7208 section 4.6.4. A change in an included record can push it over the limit without any change on your side.
finding.SPF_NEAR_LOOKUP_LIMIT.remediatio: Keep headroom below the limit: remove unused includes, replace a and mx with ip4/ip6 where the addresses are under your control, and re-check after adding a new sending service.
finding.SPF_NEAR_LOOKUP_LIMIT.title: SPF close to the DNS lookup limit
finding.SPF_NEUTRAL_ALL_SOFTFAIL.detail: The record at {name} ends with ~all: unlisted hosts get softfail, a weak statement that they are probably not authorized (RFC 7208 section 2.6.5). This is a common and valid choice.
finding.SPF_NEUTRAL_ALL_SOFTFAIL.remedia: No change is required. When you are confident every legitimate sender is listed, you can move to -all for a definitive fail result.
finding.SPF_NEUTRAL_ALL_SOFTFAIL.title: SPF default is softfail (~all)
finding.SPF_NO_ALL.detail: The record at {name} has neither an all mechanism nor a redirect, so unlisted hosts get the implicit default neutral, as if ?all were present (RFC 7208 section 4.7).
finding.SPF_NO_ALL.remediation: Add an explicit all mechanism at the end of the record, usually -all or ~all.
finding.SPF_NO_ALL.title: SPF record has no all mechanism
finding.SPF_PLUS_ALL.detail: The record at {name} ({via}) ends evaluation with +all (or a bare all), so every IP address on the internet gets SPF pass (RFC 7208 sections 2.6.3 and 5.1).
finding.SPF_PLUS_ALL.remediation: Replace +all with -all (or ~all while you are still verifying your senders) and list the authorized hosts explicitly.
finding.SPF_PLUS_ALL.title: SPF allows every host (+all)
finding.SPF_PTR_DEPRECATED.detail: The record at {name} uses ptr (see evidence). RFC 7208 section 5.5 says: "This mechanism SHOULD NOT be published." The RFC explains that it is slow, less reliable than other mechanisms when DNS errors occur, and places a large burden on the .arpa name servers.
finding.SPF_PTR_DEPRECATED.remediation: Replace ptr with ip4/ip6, a or include terms that list the sending hosts directly.
finding.SPF_PTR_DEPRECATED.title: SPF uses the ptr mechanism
finding.SPF_QUESTION_ALL.detail: The record at {name} ends with ?all: for hosts not listed, the domain explicitly asserts nothing (neutral, RFC 7208 section 2.6.2), so SPF gives receivers no protection against spoofing.
finding.SPF_QUESTION_ALL.remediation: Once all legitimate senders are listed, replace ?all with ~all or -all.
finding.SPF_QUESTION_ALL.title: SPF default is neutral (?all)
finding.SPF_RECORD_TOO_LONG.detail: The SPF data at {name} is at least {length} octets (other TXT records at the same name are not counted), above the {limit}-octet threshold. A record longer than 255 octets is valid, but it must be published as several strings of at most 255 octets each, which receivers concatenate (RFC 7208 section 3.3). RFC 7208 section 3.4 adds that the answer should fit in a 512-octet UDP message, which means keeping the name plus all records of the type under 450 octets; larger answers risk being ignored by verifiers.
finding.SPF_RECORD_TOO_LONG.remediation: Make sure a record over 255 octets is published as several quoted strings of at most 255 octets each in one TXT record. If the answer is over 450 octets, shorten the record (remove unused terms, merge address ranges).
finding.SPF_RECORD_TOO_LONG.title: SPF record is long
finding.SPF_REDIRECT_WITH_ALL.detail: The record at {name} has both an all mechanism and a redirect modifier. RFC 7208 sections 5.1 and 6.1 require receivers to ignore the redirect in that case.
finding.SPF_REDIRECT_WITH_ALL.remediatio: Remove either the redirect or the all mechanism, depending on which policy you actually want to apply.
finding.SPF_REDIRECT_WITH_ALL.title: SPF redirect is ignored
finding.SPF_RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED.detail: Resolution stopped at a safety limit after {count} DNS-querying terms; the real count is at least this high and already over the RFC 7208 limit.
finding.SPF_RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED.remedia: Reduce the number of include, a, mx, ptr, exists and redirect terms so the whole tree stays within 10 lookups.
finding.SPF_RESOLUTION_TRUNCATED.title: SPF tree too large to resolve fully
finding.SPF_SYNTAX_ERROR.detail: The SPF record at {name} is not valid per RFC 7208 (see evidence). A syntax error anywhere in the record, or a malformed target name, makes receivers return permerror (RFC 7208 sections 4.6 and 5.2).
finding.SPF_SYNTAX_ERROR.remediation: Fix or remove the terms listed in the evidence so the record follows the RFC 7208 grammar. If the record belongs to another provider, ask them to fix it or remove the include.
finding.SPF_SYNTAX_ERROR.title: SPF record has syntax errors
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_LOOKUPS.detail: Evaluating the SPF record needs {count} DNS-querying terms (include, a, mx, ptr, exists, redirect); RFC 7208 section 4.6.4 allows at most {limit}, and receivers return permerror above it.
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_LOOKUPS.remediation: Reduce the number of include, a, mx, ptr and exists terms: remove services that no longer send for the domain, replace a and mx with ip4/ip6 where the addresses are under your control, or move some senders to a subdomain with its own SPF record.
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_LOOKUPS.title: Too many SPF DNS lookups
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_VOID_LOOKUPS.detail: {count} lookups in the SPF tree return no data or a non-existent name (see evidence). RFC 7208 section 4.6.4 recommends a limit of {limit}; receivers applying it return permerror.
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_VOID_LOOKUPS.remedi: Remove or correct the terms pointing to names that do not exist or have no records of the queried type.
finding.SPF_TOO_MANY_VOID_LOOKUPS.title: Too many void SPF lookups
